subject: Request: one-line data handling snapshot + subprocessor footnote for Console card

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: one-line data handling snapshot for Redwood Console card

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — procurement at Acme Health is working through a short checklist for our security team and we could use a concise, public-facing sentence we can place in our vendor registry UI and procurement one-pager. Specifically: 

1) Can you provide a one-line “data handling snapshot” (plain-language, customer-facing) that we can show on a console card and in a procurement quicksheet?
2) We also need a short footnote (1–2 lines) that explains subprocessors and where we publish the current list (and whether you can provide a CSV of subprocessor countries for our SOC review).

Our legal/infosec contact is looping in Sarah Kim (copied) if you want an external counsel touchpoint. Ideally we can get the copy + CSV by EOD Friday 4/30.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Desai
Senior Sourcing Manager | Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Request: one-line data handling snapshot for Redwood Console card

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (privacy/legal) and Marcus (product copy) to help craft a short, customer-friendly blurb and to surface the subprocessor CSV.

Initial thought for a one-line snapshot (very rough):
"Redwood processes customer-provided text in our hosted API and uses a small set of vetted subprocessors to support hosting, logging, and billing; we do not use customer data to train models."

For the footnote we can point customers to our public subprocessor page + offer a downloadable CSV of the current subprocessors by country. Kimberly — can you advise on the phrasing that stays DPA-safe (and whether we should avoid mentioning specific hosting vendor names in the one-liner)? Marcus — can you propose a super-compact variant for the console card (30–60 characters ideally)?

I’ll draft attachments once we have legal sign-off.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <p.desai@acmehealth.com>, Sarah Kim <s.kim@consultlaw.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: one-line data handling snapshot for Redwood Console card

Thanks Lauren — quick legal note and a suggested wording set below. I attached an export of the subprocessor countries (subprocessor-countries.csv) for Acme's SOC intake.

Legal constraints: keep the one-line factual, avoid statements implying we share customer data for model training (we do not), and prefer generic functional descriptions over vendor brand names in public short copy. For procurement/legal packets we can provide a separate table with vendor names and subprocessor roles.

Suggested public-facing options (choose one):
A) Short (console card): "We process customer text in our hosted API and use approved subprocessors to run and secure the service; we do not use customer data to train models."
B) Concise footnote (1–2 lines): "Subprocessors perform hosting, logging, monitoring, and billing on Redwood's behalf. The current subprocessor list and country export are available here: [link]. Customers may request an export for procurement."

If Acme prefers including a transparency link instead of a CSV in the console card, we should link to the console tooltip/drive doc (I added the drive link in related_links).

Attachments: subprocessor-countries.csv (country-level export for procurement intake).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <p.desai@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: one-line data handling snapshot for Redwood Console card

Picking up Kimberly's options — for the console card we really want to maximize scannability. My two cents: shorten A to the tightest possible UX line and put the verifier detail in the tooltip/footnote.

Proposed console card copy (30–60 chars):
"We process customer text; approved subprocessors support the service."

Tooltip / footnote (display on hover or small link):
"Subprocessors perform hosting, logging, monitoring, and billing. See current list and country export: [link]."

If legal is comfortable, we can keep this live copy and attach the CSV to procurement. Lauren — happy to mock the card and the tooltip copy and export a PDF for Acme.

—Marcus
Product Content Lead
marcus_lin@redwood.com
